title: Joint Adaptive Quantile Network VAR and Connectedness-Adjusted Portfolio Allocation: Evidence from Cryptocurrency Markets
content: This study connects jointly estimated conditional-quantile networks with cryptocurrency portfolio allocation. A joint adaptive quantile network VAR (JAQN–VAR) represents cross-asset lag coefficients through quadratic B-splines over seven quantiles, combining adaptive group shrinkage, curvature regularization and soft noncrossing control. Normalized generalized forecast-error variance decomposition supplies directional transmitter scores to a connectedness-adjusted minimum-variance (CAMV) portfolio. BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP and ADA are modeled using 2,479 training observations and a matched 620-day evaluation with five-day rebalancing and transaction costs. Static q05 JAQN–CAMV earns −5.204% cumulative net return versus −5.640% for minimum variance, −15.373% for minimum CVaR and −32.621% for equal weighting; however, minimum CVaR records the lowest volatility and expected shortfall, and the mean-return difference versus minimum variance is statistically inconclusive. Updating the network every five days using a 1,000-observation rolling window yields −5.041% cumulative return. In known-oracle location-shift simulations (160 datasets per quantile), JAQN–VAR reduces GFEVD Edge MAE versus exact QVAR by 6.33%, 0.58% and 5.55% at q05, q50 and q95. Advantages versus separately penalized QVAR are conditional, and quantile-varying location–scale designs expose lower- and upper-tail failure modes. The findings support a feasible dynamic network-to-portfolio workflow, not uniform estimator or risk dominance.
